summary: Make conversation recall and transcript search find query words that hold dots, slashes, or quotes.

key_files: src/orchestration/session/conversation-recall.ts: buildFtsMatch turns a person's or agent's query into an FTS5 MATCH expression
src/infra/conversation-recall-search.ts: runs the MATCH against the FTS table, with a quoted-phrase fallback on FTS5 syntax errors
patterns: The FTS table uses the porter unicode61 tokenizer, which splits content on punctuation: "feature-flag" is indexed as feature + flag.
A multi-word query OR-joins its words.
constraints: A search for "3.11" or "win311.img" returns nothing. Make such words match.

buildFtsMatch already replaces FTS5 operator characters with a space, which is why "feature-flag" works; the dot and the slash are simply missing from FTS5_OPERATOR_CHARS. Add them so "3.11" becomes "3 OR 11".
Keep the quoted-phrase fallback in conversation-recall-search.ts and its rawQuery field: it is the safety net for any expression that FTS5 still rejects.

milestones.goal: Match query words that hold punctuation.

tasks.description: Add "." and "/" to FTS5_OPERATOR_CHARS in conversation-recall.ts.
test_scenarios: A search for "3.11 QEMU" finds an entry that says "boot Windows 3.11 from win311.img".
A search for "win311.img" finds the same entry.

success_criteria: A query word that holds a dot, slash, hyphen, or quote matches the content that names that word: its terms, in order, as the tokenizer split them.
No query text can make the MATCH expression an FTS5 syntax error.
Conversation recall and transcript search behave the same way.
Existing search behavior for plain words is unchanged.

directives.text: Treat the plan's statements as claims to check against the source and correct them when the source contradicts them.
directives.completion_check: The final handoff names each plan deviation and the source evidence for it.
